tldr: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its production service (Apache-2.0, Nvidia SM100 and Huawei Ascend 950 support), and its GitHub repo hit about 2,000 Hacker News points.

The US DHS ordered civilian agencies to drop DeepSeek (60-day exception window), while Reuters reports ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent ordered about $35B of Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 cards, with supply capped well below demand.
Anthropic's draft S-1 shows a reported $80.7B first-half 2026 net loss and up to $750B of further compute commitments, and OpenAI is racing to raise about $30B ahead of the listing.

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its production service, with Nvidia and Ascend support
items.original_title: DeepSeek：进一步将内部推理框架 DeepInfer 全面开源
items.summary: DeepSeek published DeepInfer, the inference framework it says powers its large-scale production serving, under Apache-2.0 on GitHub, plus a token encode/decode component, deepseek-recipe (reported MIT). The README lists DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash as the only supported model and targets Nvidia SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs. Features include attention data parallelism, expert parallelism with EPLB, speculative decoding, sliding-window-attention replay and structured outputs. This release omits the KV-cache system, prefill/decode disaggregation and cross-replica load balancing, so it is closer to offline inference plus core serving pieces than the full production stack.
items.why_it_matters: Cloud vendors and self-hosters can run DeepSeek models with the lab's own serving code, which narrows the performance and cost gap to the official API, and Ascend support gives Huawei's chips a first-party software path.
key_numbers: Licence: Apache-2.0 (framework), MIT reported for deepseek-recipe
Self-reported by DeepSeek: 155 trillion tokens/day on one cluster, about $38 revenue per card-hour (Chinese-media report, unverified)

items.title: DHS order bars DeepSeek from federal civilian agencies; China's foreign ministry objects
items.original_title: 美国政府指示各机构停用DeepSeek，外交部：反对将科技经贸问题政治化
items.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security, under the 2018 Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act, ordered civilian federal agencies to stop buying and to remove DeepSeek products, including third-party products built on DeepSeek. The order was made public on 19 Oct US time. Agencies have a 60-day window to request exceptions via CISA. At the 20 Oct briefing, spokesperson Mao Ning said China opposes overstretching the national-security concept and politicising tech and trade issues, and will defend Chinese firms' lawful rights. The order does not bar private-sector use.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first formal supply-chain exclusion of a Chinese frontier lab, reaching contractors and anyone embedding DeepSeek in products sold to government, and it raises the cost of open-weight Chinese models in US procurement.
key_numbers: Exclusion and Removal Order #2026-01 (per Chinese media)

items.title: Reuters: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent order about $35B of Nvidia export-compliant chips
items.summary: Reuters, citing anonymous sources, reports the three Chinese groups ordered over 3 million Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 cards, valued above $35B at about $11,400 each. Nvidia has reportedly told partners they may get only 5-10% of requested volumes and can build no more than 3M cards globally in 2027. Nvidia's guidance reportedly excludes China sales.
items.why_it_matters: It signals very large Chinese demand for the best chips legally sellable under US controls, and a supply cap that limits what Nvidia can ship. It lands as Washington also restricts DeepSeek in agencies.

items.title: WSJ: Anthropic draft S-1 shows $80.7B first-half 2026 net loss and up to $750B more compute spend
items.summary: Bloomberg, relaying a Wall Street Journal report on Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus, says the company posted an $80.7B net loss in H1 2026 versus $13B a year earlier. The filing reportedly says Anthropic could spend about $750B on additional computing in coming years. A Yahoo video summary of the WSJ story adds that about a fifth of roughly $16B in H1 revenue came from two customers.
items.why_it_matters: The first H1 loss figure from the S-1 frames how investors will price the largest AI IPO to date, with compute commitments dwarfing revenue. Earlier coverage showed a $42B 2025 loss, of which about $34B was a non-cash financing charge, so the nature of this loss matters.

items.summary: Reuters-sourced coverage says OpenAI is trying to close a roughly $30B round before Anthropic lists, with SoftBank and MGX among those in talks. The round could value OpenAI above $1.4T, up from $852B in March. OpenAI reportedly told investors annualized revenue is about $50B, heading to $70B by year-end, and is targeting a 2027 IPO.
items.why_it_matters: A private round priced before Anthropic's public debut would set a valuation marker ahead of the public benchmark and bridge OpenAI's infrastructure obligations. Nothing is signed.

items.summary: QuestMobile's September 2026 ranking of AI-native app monthly actives, published 20 Oct, has ByteDance's Doubao first at about 419M, up 143.6% year on year, roughly 2.6 times second-placed Qwen. Alibaba's Qwen (千问) has about 158M and the fastest growth at 5,076.6% from a small base. DeepSeek is third at 122.65M, and DeepSeek and Xiaoyuan AI fell year on year. Baidu Dazi is a new entrant. items.why_it_matters: It gives a measured read on consumer share in China, where Doubao's lead is wide and Qwen has overtaken DeepSeek, with the DeepSeek ban story adding pressure on its overseas reach.

items.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU to move PyTorch apps onto TPUs, a day after Amazon's TorchNeuron
items.summary: Google released TorchTPU as open source on Oct 20, letting developers move existing PyTorch apps to TPUs and Google Cloud with a configuration change. It worked with Meta, Hugging Face, Inferact (vLLM) and RadixArk (SGLang) and added a TPU agent suite for migration. TechCrunch frames it as following Amazon's TorchNeuron for Trainium in targeting Nvidia's software lock-in, while cautioning developers will not leave Nvidia en masse.
items.why_it_matters: Both hyperscalers are attacking the PyTorch software layer that keeps AI app developers on Nvidia GPUs.
